Articles.generativeAIDisclosure.paragrap: We live in a world where AI-based tools are used in most software projects and in everyday life. Whether it's brainstorming ideas, discussing art concepts, getting coding assistance, or proofreading texts, you can expect AI to be used in most projects. Steam stopped asking game developers to disclose general AI usage since everyone would say yes and limited the question to whether the game has AI-generated assets the player can directly see. We will adopt the same approach.

The goal of this page is to let players know where and how we use generative AI. We believe in transparency. This should help us avoid cases where we are wrongly accused of using generative AI even though we invested a lot of time and energy to deliver the best quality.

We use AI-powered tools to speed up feature development and for code reviews to catch potential issues before they are faced by players. For graphical assets, we typically start with AI-based concept generation so we can have discussions within the team about which direction we want to go and to explore ideas. The final graphical assets are created manually because current AI tools are not good enough for the quality we want.

Generative AI for text has enabled us to build features we could not before. We can quickly check chat posts for obvious rules violations. We can translate newspaper articles that were previously available only in English. We can understand bug reports written in other languages. We use AI translation in the user interface as a placeholder until a person can provide the high-quality translation.

To sum up: We use AI extensively as part of our toolset. We rarely use AI-generated content directly, except where player use is limited or the feature would not exist otherwise, because it would be too expensive for the size of our team and our non-pay-to-win pricing.

Audit.intro: The Fair Play Association's main goal is to ensure the same, fair, game play conditions for all companies. All players should have access to the same resources at similar prices. Obtaining resources at prices significantly lower than the rest of the players, or selling resources at a premium significantly higher than the rest of the players, by means of creating more than one account is against the rules. It gives the company an unfair advantage against the rest of the players. Each player is allowed to create and control only one company and must execute trades in a way that is fair to all companies within the game's economy.

Contest.contestDetails: Contest details and rules will be available after the contest starts.
Contest.rulesB: The first company to deliver is the winner, the next 4 companies will get certificates. The winner also receives {winnerXp} XP, and every other certificate recipient receives {certificateXp} XP.
Contest.rulesD: The contest is broken down into checkpoints. At each checkpoint, the {contestants} companies who donated the most since the last checkpoint get points. The company that donated most gets {contestants} points, the one at the 2nd position gets {contestants_less_one} points, and likewise. At the end of the contest, the company with most points wins. The {contestants} companies with most points get certificates. The winner also receives {winnerXp} XP, and every other certificate recipient receives {certificateXp} XP.
Contest.rulesP: The contest is broken down into checkpoints. At each checkpoint, the top 10 companies at that moment get points. The company that is leading in the amount donated gets 10 points, the one at the 2nd position gets 9 points, and likewise. At the end of the contest, the company with most points wins. The 10 companies with most points get certificates. The winner also receives {winnerXp} XP, and every other certificate recipient receives {certificateXp} XP.
Contest.rulesR: The contest is broken down into checkpoints. At each checkpoint, the {contestants} companies who made the most profit of restaurants since the last checkpoint get points. The company with most profit gets {contestants} points, the one at the 2nd position gets {contestants_less_one} points, and likewise. At the end of the contest, the company with most points wins. The {contestants} companies with most points get certificates. The winner also receives {winnerXp} XP, and every other certificate recipient receives {certificateXp} XP.
Contest.ties: Ties are broken by using the time of the last contest donation. The sooner the better.

Home.about3: We believe the best stuff in life is free! At the beginning, there was no point in charging anything — it was just Patrik and a few friends playing, and server costs were negligible.
Home.about4: However, the game now depends on many third-party services that are only free when traffic is low. With our current player base, the server infrastructure needs to handle over 200 requests per second. It is not possible to keep Sim Companies running without some form of monetization. With that said, our intent is to keep Sim Companies free to play for everyone who does not want to spend money.
Home.about5: Thank you for your support — it helps us maintain the servers, improve the game, and keep building new features.
Home.aboutStory1: Sim Companies started as a hobby project in late 2015. I wanted to play a business simulation game, but I couldn't find one I liked. I had a working concept by the start of 2016, purchased the domain, and slowly added more and more features. I got a few friends to play with me, which helped me discover a lot of early bugs and helped shape the economy. They also pointed out that the graphics could use some improvement, so I hired freelancers to help me out in areas where I lacked the necessary skills.
Home.aboutStory2: In September 2017, the game started landing high in the Google search results, and we started getting real traffic and the player base grew. It was like a switch had flipped. This was incredibly exciting, as all the work I put into the game now had more meaning. The fact that other people were enjoying something I created filled me with joy. I am incredibly lucky that what started as a hobby project of mine turned into something players want to support, allowing me to work on it full-time and build a dream team to help out.

Home.coolThings: One of the incredibly realistic features you get to experience is the live, ever-changing, free market. Guess if the price of a certain resource will go up or down? Would you like to take a risk? Maybe you can trigger a certain price change yourself. Understanding the market dynamics is a very useful skill for someone to have. Players can, and the game too influences them to exchange resources among themselves. Players can also specialize in certain parts of the resource chain which yields the most profit. It is also challenging for the user to find the right business partners and negotiate prices. The (supplier-consumer) relationship is further supported by the Sim Companies concept of contracts where companies interested in or with long term relationships can exchange resources directly, saving on market fees.

Home.measureYourSkills: Do you want to measure your skills against other players in a virtual economy? Do you want to own a production, retail or research company which pays out the best? It all depends on the current conditions in the virtual economy and how skillful you are in spotting business opportunities. Sim Companies is an extremely versatile browser game that allows you to experiment with various resources and test your skills against other players in the game. Sim Companies is a business simulation strategy game aimed at giving you the fun and experience of managing a company using real world economic principles. The goal of the game is to create a profitable and competitive business. Each player receives a starting capital and few assets. Players' day-to-day tasks consist of managing the resource supply chain, from production to selling in retail, procuring business partners, ensuring financing, etc. For players to prosper, they would have to be able to read market conditions and take some trading shortcuts here and there, maybe buy their input resources on market cheaper than if they produced them or sell them on the market with higher profit than in the retail. When should players invest into research? We thought about what makes company management fun and what makes it tedious. Sim companies' philosophy is to let you take the interesting decisions while building your own business without having to fill in tons of extra settings. We do not want to simulate the real world with all its law and other restrictions, but rather give players the freedom to make decisions that can impact their company finances and value.
Home.peoplePlaying: People playing Sim Companies are gaining knowledge and improving their skills in teamwork, business operations, leadership, and business development. Learning by active involvement is an established method that guarantees long term skill retention. The game rewards players with achievement badges. Companies are rewarded for employing people, building infrastructure, making profits off the market and other activities. This gratification ensures positive feedback when the right decisions are taken and provides good and viable short term goals when starting your business from scratch. This is similar to government incentives for small businesses that you would expect in the real world. Sim Companies gets its edge from an advanced economic model that simulates retail industry response to the supply and pricing that virtual companies provide. The players have control over quantity and price when offering goods in their stores. Retail parameters of all players are combined to simulate how fast the goods sold. Players can withdraw from selling for a period of time to temporarily increase the demand which would allow them to sell at higher rates later. There's no linear path to success, the decisions are good and bad based on current market and retail conditions. There's no sure strategy of winning and even if you found the right strategy, there are always ways to improve it. More importantly, if other players find your strategy; it will become less and less profitable, especially if everyone starts using it.

hq.banana.description: Is it an apple? Is it a pineapple? No! It's a banana! Transform your HQ into a barbie dream house now.
hq.default.description: What everyone else has: Not great, not terrible.
hq.golf.description: And why not? It's great to play a bit of golf during the lunch break. Your employees will love to get sunburned on green grass roof.
hq.golf2.description: Yes, higher is always better, play golf in style looking at the city below.
hq.greenTower.description: There's never enough green in cities, set an example with HQ that will transform the look of the city!
hq.haunted.description: Spooooky .. Yes, it's true, we found a way to scare off those annoying sales people trying to sell us insurance.

hq.kyiv.description: Show your support for nation under attack ... :(
hq.obsidian.description: Nothing says 'serious business' like a menacing black fortress that makes even your toughest competitors think twice.
hq.vintage.description: Travel into the past and use the good old HQ from the beginning of time.
hq.winter.description: Spread the Xmas cheer by allowing your employees to work from a magical winter cabin-like HQ. Every office is fitted with a real fireplace.
hq.xmas.description: Who doesn't love the Xmas atmosphere on the city square under the Xmas tree?
